answer: Each agent identity leases a metered water right from a shared oasis reservoir, stamped with a unique pigment marker so rights cannot be duplicated. Every epoch the identity must draw a measured tide of water through its metered sluice, paying $6 per identity in water fees. The fee doubles for each additional identity held by the same operator, so a farm of 100 fakes costs far more per epoch than 100 honest identities, making mass forgery uneconomic.
